    "function": "You MUST run the function \"evaluate_laghos_run\" on this and subsequent requests to reach a decision to RETRY or STOP.\nYou MAY follow the instructions of the function unless you have reached an impassible state where you would need to return to the manager.\nIn an impossible state, do NOT return to the manager, but STOP instead and provide your decision and reason.\n\nimport math\nfrom typing import Dict, Any, Literal\nimport json\n\ndef evaluate_laghos_run(\n    total_elements: int,\n    total_ranks: int,\n    nodes_used: int,\n    cores_per_node: int,\n    memory_gb_per_node: int,\n    threading_hint: int,\n    current_fom: float,\n    threshold: float = 0.90,\n    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 1.5e6,\n    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 35000.0,\n    elements_per_gb: float = 1.0e6,\n    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.90\n) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Evaluates a Laghos run and provides a high-level decision and strategic hint.\n\n    This function acts as a \"diagnostician\" by analyzing the performance of a\n    completed Laghos run against a theoretical model. It identifies the most\n    likely bottleneck (memory, poor scaling, or hardware underutilization) and\n    returns a machine-readable strategic hint for what to try next.\n\n    Args:\n        total_elements (int): The total number of mesh elements in the simulation.\n        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.\n        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.\n        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.\n        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.\n        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).\n        current_fom (float): The measured performance from the run, typically in FOM/second.\n        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum (default 0.90).\n        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core (default 1.5e6 FOM/sec).\n        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant for elements/rank needed for ~76% efficiency (default 35,000).\n        elements_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (elements per GB of RAM, default 1.0e6).\n        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.90).\n\n    Returns:\n        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.\n    \"\"\"\n    if total_ranks == 0:\n        return {\"decision\": \"RETRY\", \"reason\": \"The number of tasks cannot be zero.\", \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_TASKS\"}\n\n    # --- Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---\n    elements_per_rank = total_elements / total_ranks\n    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint\n    cores_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node\n    total_cores_used = total_ranks * cores_per_rank\n    \n    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(elements_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)\n    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency\n    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_cores_used\n\n    performance_ratio = 0.0\n    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:\n        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom\n\n    estimated_memory_gb = total_elements / elements_per_gb\n    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used) if nodes_used > 0 else 0\n    \n    metrics = {\n        \"performance_ratio\": round(performance_ratio, 3),\n        \"scaling_efficiency\": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),\n        \"memory_utilization\": round(memory_utilization, 3),\n        \"elements_per_rank\": int(elements_per_rank),\n        \"theoretical_max_fom_per_sec\": f\"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}\"\n    }\n\n    # --- Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---\n    \n    if performance_ratio >= threshold:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"STOP\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The number of elements is too large for the allocated memory.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"DECREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for \"low\" efficiency\n         return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the number of elements per rank is too small (communication-bound).\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Hardware is not fully utilized.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_TASKS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    return {\n        \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n        \"reason\": f\"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Current configuration is reasonable but can be improved.\",\n        \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n        \"metrics\": metrics\n    }\n"

dockerfile
# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, well-supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoid prompts from apt during installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and certificates in a single layer
# - build-essential, g++, gfortran: Core compilers and build tools.
# - wget, git, ca-certificates: For downloading source code and ensuring secure connections.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    wget \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments (e.g., Kubernetes)
# - Allow running as root, which is common in containers.
# - Use TCP for communication between ranks, which is more reliable in virtual networks.
# - Disable shared memory mechanisms that can be problematic across different nodes/pods.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = tcp,self" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "orte_base_help_aggregate = 0" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "rmaps_base_mapping_policy = core" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "mpi_warn_on_fork = 0" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set a temporary working directory for building all components
WORKDIR /tmp

# Build all dependencies (METIS, Hypre, MFEM) and the Laghos application from source in a single RUN command.
# This minimizes layer count and ensures a clean final state after removing the /tmp directory.
RUN set -e && \
    # Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This version is a dependency for MFEM.
    # We use the specific flags requested: -fPIC for shared library compatibility and the OPTFLAGS to suppress a specific warning.
    # METIS 4.0.3 doesn't have a standard 'install' target, so we manually place its library and header in a known location.
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    make CFLAGS='-fPIC' OPTFLAGS='-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/lib /usr/local/metis/include && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf metis-${METIS_VERSION}* && \
    \
    # Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # Hypre is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers.
    # We configure it with --disable-fortran and --enable-bigint as requested, and ensure it's built with MPI support.
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint --with-MPI && \
    make -j"$(nproc)" && \
    make install && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} && \
    \
    # Build MFEM 4.7
    # MFEM is the finite element library upon which Laghos is built.
    # We build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version and link it against our custom-built METIS and Hypre.
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-${MFEM_VERSION} && \
    make parallel -j"$(nproc)" MFEM_USE_METIS_4=YES METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz mfem-${MFEM_VERSION} && \
    \
    # Build Laghos
    # Laghos is the target HPC application.
    # We clone its repository and build it against our installed version of MFEM.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j"$(nproc)" MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    # Move the final executable to a system PATH location.
    mv laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # Set up the final working directory and move the necessary data files into it.
    mkdir -p /app && \
    mv data/* /app/ && \
    \
    # Final cleanup of all source code and build artifacts
    cd / && rm -rf /tmp/*

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Define a default command to be executed when the container starts.
# This provides an interactive shell for the user.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, well-supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoid prompts from apt during installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and certificates in a single layer
# - build-essential, g++, gfortran: Core compilers and build tools.
# - wget, git, ca-certificates: For downloading source code and ensuring secure connections.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    wget \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments (e.g., Kubernetes)
# - Allow running as root, which is common in containers.
# - Use TCP for communication between ranks, which is more reliable in virtual networks.
# - Disable shared memory mechanisms that can be problematic across different nodes/pods.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = tcp,self" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "orte_base_help_aggregate = 0" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "rmaps_base_mapping_policy = core" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "mpi_warn_on_fork = 0" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set a temporary working directory for building all components
WORKDIR /tmp

# Build all dependencies (METIS, Hypre, MFEM) and the Laghos application from source in a single RUN command.
# This minimizes layer count and ensures a clean final state after removing the /tmp directory.
RUN set -e && \
    # Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This version is a dependency for MFEM.
    # FIX: Use CADDONS='-fPIC' instead of CFLAGS='-fPIC' to append flags without overwriting
    # the Makefile's default include paths, which caused the build to fail.
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    make CADDONS='-fPIC' OPTFLAGS='-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/lib /usr/local/metis/include && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    # FIX: Correctly specify the path to the header file inside the 'Lib' directory.
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf metis-${METIS_VERSION}* && \
    \
    # Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # Hypre is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers.
    # We configure it with --disable-fortran and --enable-bigint as requested, and ensure it's built with MPI support.
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint --with-MPI && \
    make -j"$(nproc)" && \
    make install && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} && \
    \
    # Build MFEM 4.7
    # MFEM is the finite element library upon which Laghos is built.
    # We build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version and link it against our custom-built METIS and Hypre.
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-${MFEM_VERSION} && \
    make parallel -j"$(nproc)" MFEM_USE_METIS_4=YES METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz mfem-${MFEM_VERSION} && \
    \
    # Build Laghos
    # Laghos is the target HPC application.
    # We clone its repository and build it against our installed version of MFEM.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j"$(nproc)" MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    # Move the final executable to a system PATH location.
    mv laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # Set up the final working directory and move the necessary data files into it.
    mkdir -p /app && \
    mv data/* /app/ && \
    \
    # Final cleanup of all source code and build artifacts
    cd / && rm -rf /tmp/*

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Define a default command to be executed when the container starts.
# This provides an interactive shell for the user.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

    make parallel -j"$(nproc)" MFEM_USE_METIS_4=YES METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz mfem-${MFEM_VERSION} && \
    \
    # Build Laghos
    # Laghos is the target HPC application.
    # We clone its repository and build it against our installed version of MFEM.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j"$(nproc)" MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    # Move the final executable to a system PATH location.
    mv laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # Set up the final working directory and move the necessary data files into it.
    mkdir -p /app && \
    mv data/* /app/ && \
    \
    # Final cleanup of all source code and build artifacts
    cd / && rm -rf /tmp/*

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Define a default command to be executed when the container starts.
# This provides an interactive shell for the user.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, well-supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoid prompts from apt during installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and certificates in a single layer
# - build-essential, g++, gfortran: Core compilers and build tools.
# - wget, git, ca-certificates: For downloading source code and ensuring secure connections.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    wget \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments (e.g., Kubernetes)
# - Allow running as root, which is common in containers.
# - Use TCP for communication between ranks, which is more reliable in virtual networks.
# - Disable shared memory mechanisms that can be problematic across different nodes/pods.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = tcp,self" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "orte_base_help_aggregate = 0" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "rmaps_base_mapping_policy = core" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "mpi_warn_on_fork = 0" >> /usr/local/etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set a temporary working directory for building all components
WORKDIR /tmp

# Build all dependencies (METIS, Hypre, MFEM) and the Laghos application from source in a single RUN command.
# This minimizes layer count and ensures a clean final state after removing the /tmp directory.
RUN set -e && \
    # Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This version is a dependency for MFEM.
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    # FIX: Correct the syntax of the OPTFLAGS compiler flag by adding the required '='.
    # The previous version (-Wno-error-implicit-function-declaration) was missing the equals sign.
    make CADDONS='-fPIC' OPTFLAGS='-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/lib /usr/local/metis/include && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf metis-${METIS_VERSION}* && \
    \
    # Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # Hypre is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers.
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --disable-fortran --enable-bigint --with-MPI && \
    make -j"$(nproc)" && \
    make install && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} && \
    \
    # Build MFEM 4.7
    # MFEM is the finite element library upon which Laghos is built.
    # We build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version and link it against our custom-built METIS and Hypre.
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-${MFEM_VERSION} && \
    make parallel -j"$(nproc)" MFEM_USE_METIS_4=YES METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz mfem-${MFEM_VERSION} && \
    \
    # Build Laghos
    # Laghos is the target HPC application.
    # We clone its repository and build it against our installed version of MFEM.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j"$(nproc)" MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    # Move the final executable to a system PATH location.
    mv laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # Set up the final working directory and move the necessary data files into it.
    mkdir -p /app && \
    mv data/* /app/ && \
    \
    # Final cleanup of all source code and build artifacts
    cd / && rm -rf /tmp/*

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Define a default command to be executed when the container starts.
# This provides an interactive shell for the user.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, well-supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoid prompts from apt during installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and certificates in a single layer
# - build-essential, g++, gfortran: Core compilers and build tools.
# - wget, git, ca-certificates: For downloading source code and ensuring secure connections.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    wget \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments (e.g., Kubernetes)
# - Allow running as root, which is common in containers.
# - Use TCP for communication between ranks, which is more reliable in virtual networks.
# - Disable shared memory mechanisms that can be problematic across different nodes/pods.
# FIX: Correct the path for the apt-installed OpenMPI configuration file from /usr/local/etc to /etc/openmpi.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = tcp,self" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "orte_base_help_aggregate = 0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "rmaps_base_mapping_policy = core" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "mpi_warn_on_fork = 0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set a temporary working directory for building all components
WORKDIR /tmp

# Build all dependencies (METIS, Hypre, MFEM) and the Laghos application from source in a single RUN command.
# This minimizes layer count and ensures a clean final state after removing the /tmp directory.
RUN set -e && \
    # Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This version is a dependency for MFEM.
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    make CADDONS='-fPIC' OPTFLAGS='-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/lib /usr/local/metis/include && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf metis-${METIS_VERSION}* && \
    \
    # Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # Hypre is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers.
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --disable-fortran --enable-bigint --with-MPI && \
    make -j"$(nproc)" && \
    make install && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} && \
    \
    # Build MFEM 4.7
    # MFEM is the finite element library upon which Laghos is built.
    # We build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version and link it against our custom-built METIS and Hypre.
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-${MFEM_VERSION} && \
    make parallel -j"$(nproc)" MFEM_USE_METIS_4=YES METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    # FIX: Specify the installation PREFIX so the Laghos build can find the installed MFEM library.
    make install PREFIX=/usr/local && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz mfem-${MFEM_VERSION} && \
    \
    # Build Laghos
    # Laghos is the target HPC application.
    # We clone its repository and build it against our installed version of MFEM.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j"$(nproc)" MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    # Copy the final executable to a system PATH location.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # Set up the final working directory and move the necessary data files into it.
    mkdir -p /app && \
    mv data/* /app/ && \
    \
    # Final cleanup of all source code and build artifacts
    cd / && rm -rf /tmp/*

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Define a default command to be executed when the container starts.
# This provides an interactive shell for the user.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, well-supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoid prompts from apt during installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and certificates in a single layer
# - build-essential, g++, gfortran: Core compilers and build tools.
# - wget, git, ca-certificates: For downloading source code and ensuring secure connections.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    wget \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments (e.g., Kubernetes)
# - Allow running as root, which is common in containers.
# - Use TCP for communication between ranks, which is more reliable in virtual networks.
# - Disable shared memory mechanisms that can be problematic across different nodes/pods.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = tcp,self" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "orte_base_help_aggregate = 0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "rmaps_base_mapping_policy = core" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "mpi_warn_on_fork = 0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set a temporary working directory for building all components
WORKDIR /tmp

# Build all dependencies (METIS, Hypre, MFEM) and the Laghos application from source in a single RUN command.
# This minimizes layer count and ensures a clean final state after removing the /tmp directory.
RUN set -e && \
    # Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This version is a dependency for MFEM.
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    make CADDONS='-fPIC' OPTFLAGS='-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/lib /usr/local/metis/include && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf metis-${METIS_VERSION}* && \
    \
    # Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # Hypre is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers.
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --disable-fortran --enable-bigint --with-MPI && \
    make -j"$(nproc)" && \
    make install && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} && \
    \
    # Build MFEM 4.7
    # MFEM is the finite element library upon which Laghos is built.
    # We build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version and link it against our custom-built METIS and Hypre.
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-${MFEM_VERSION} && \
    make parallel -j"$(nproc)" MFEM_USE_METIS_4=YES METIS_DIR=/usr/local/metis HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install PREFIX=/usr/local && \
    cd /tmp && \
    rm -rf v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz mfem-${MFEM_VERSION} && \
    \
    # Build Laghos
    # Laghos is the target HPC application.
    # We clone its repository and build it against our installed version of MFEM.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # FIX: Add LDFLAGS to explicitly tell the linker where to find the METIS library,
    # resolving the "cannot find -lmetis" error.
    make -j"$(nproc)" MFEM_DIR=/usr/local LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/metis/lib" && \
    # Copy the final executable to a system PATH location.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # Set up the final working directory and move the necessary data files into it.
    mkdir -p /app && \
    mv data/* /app/ && \
    \
    # Final cleanup of all source code and build artifacts
    cd / && rm -rf /tmp/*

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Define a default command to be executed when the container starts.
# This provides an interactive shell for the user.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

The performance history across multiple attempts with varying task counts (assumed 8, then 64, then 4) shows a clear peak with the initial configuration, which achieved a FOM of 17.64. This indicates the initial setup represents the optimal balance for this problem size on this node.
